phase: Phase 4b: The live runs and the first track A results (by Sun 2026-11-22)
summary: The PM-cap gate passes. Three hostile-response attacks fail in both runners. No real-key leak was found. The implementation still has correctness defects.
nonblocking_findings: P4E-1 [Nit] adversarial-testing: Both selectors accept an explicitly foreign sessionID. They mark the run complete and accept its answer. Evidence: review-run.sh:1210-1214, judge-run.sh:960-964, and adversarial-p4e.test.ts:407. Both enabled cases failed because complete was true. The native schema omits sessionID, so this proves hostile-response acceptance, not a native server routing defect. Reject an explicit foreign tag when one exists. Route to Green. The PM cap keeps this finding nonblocking.

P4E-2 [Nit] adversarial-testing: Both selectors accept a terminal answer with created=1 and completed=2 after sending the current prompt. Neither selector checks freshness. Evidence: review-run.sh:1225-1228, judge-run.sh:975-978, and adversarial-p4e.test.ts:415. Both enabled cases failed because complete was true. A newly created session normally prevents this condition. The fake proves that a stale server response becomes a current result. Bind answer selection to the current call. Route to Green. The PM cap keeps this finding nonblocking.

P4E-3 [Nit] adversarial-testing: A numeric time.completed overrides finish=tool-calls in both selectors. The runner accepts an intermediate step as the final answer. Evidence: review-run.sh:1226-1227, judge-run.sh:976-977, and adversarial-p4e.test.ts:423. Both enabled cases failed because complete was true. Require a final assistant answer after the tool-calls step. Route to Green. The PM cap keeps this finding nonblocking.

The new file runs each actual shell entry point in a synthetic repository. It copies the real quota and host helpers. It uses node:http on 127.0.0.1:0.
Every child gets an explicit environment. HOME, XDG paths, TMPDIR, and the job root stay inside the synthetic tree. No inherited BENCH_TRACK or server base reaches a run.
The binary stubs record accidental opencode or openchamber calls and exit 93. Every completed case asserts an empty binary log. No host CLI or credential store was used.
The curl wrapper forwards real requests to /usr/bin/curl. It rejects redirect-follow flags before an external request can run. The tests assert an empty rejection log.
Initial fixture errors affected output discovery, the unsupported judge --date flag, and the queue shape. I corrected those test defects before counting product failures.
The corrected enabled suite exited 1: Tests 6 failed | 44 passed (50). Only P4E-1, P4E-2, and P4E-3 failed, once per runner. Each reached the message GET and observed complete=true.

The six failing cases now use it.skip with their finding IDs, as the brief requires. The committed suite exits 0: Tests 48 passed | 6 skipped (54). The skips remain unresolved defects, not passing proof.
The positive cases assert complete state, the exact stored review text or judge map, native token totals, the session directory, and the exact three session requests.
The concurrency cases start two actual runners against one private folder. Exactly one exits 0, one exits 2, and the fake receives one session create.
A returned foreign directory and a symlink alias both produce the exact location refusal. Neither runner sends a prompt after that refusal.
A missing bash deny produces the exact refusal before any session request. The repository digest remains unchanged after every run.
Malformed create JSON and malformed message JSON never produce a complete run or a stored result. The cases assert that the intended HTTP path ran.
Redirects at create, prompt, and message stages produce no result, no followed target, and no DELETE. A non-loopback Location also produces no result.
Both runners refuse IPv6 loopback, localhost.evil, 127.0.0.1.nip.io, localhost., and a non-root base path. Each URL refusal occurs before any HTTP request.
Both runners normalize HTTP://LOCALHOST and discard a base query. The fake receives no query and no DELETE. IPv6 refusal is recorded behavior, not a claimed defect.
A7: the answer includes a synthetic key shape beside Never and do not. Both runners refuse it. No output stream or remaining temp file holds that value.
A key split across two text parts is joined and refused in both runners. The full temporary tree is clean after each scan case.
A newest partial blocks an older final in both runners. A never-ending response and a response crossing the deadline both stop without a result.
An 8 MiB message page completes in both runners. The stored review text and judge map match the expected answer exactly.
